title: Review: mail/imap/auth crates Round 10
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — The biggest risk is the two-crate auth config split (IMAP vs stoa-auth) that will confuse operators. The date filter format bug (RFC 2822 vs RFC 3339) will silently return wrong results for all real data. The IMAP dummy hash cost mismatch is a timing oracle. None are immediately exploitable remotely given the typical deployment model, but they are real bugs.
Confidence: 25% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty driven by: (1) did not read the stoa-core ipld types fully to verify ArticleRootNode serialization edge cases, (2) did not check what list_groups() returns for empty groups precisely (the exact type of lo/hi as i64 vs u64 matters for the underflow finding), (3) the IMAP imap_flags DB table is created but never written by the current STORE handler (all flags go to user_flags in the mail crate) — unclear if this is intentional dead schema. Would raise confidence if: ran cargo test --workspace and observed which tests currently pass/fail, and confirmed list_groups() return type from stoa-reader.
